question: A developer keeps invoking a skill that walks the entire codebase and prints a long dependency analysis. Even after the skill finishes, this lengthy output keeps consuming space in the main conversation for the rest of the session. What frontmatter change would keep this analysis out of the main conversation's context while still returning a summary?
options: A) Add allowed-tools: Read Grep to the skill's frontmatter so the analysis is limited to read-only tools that produce shorter output.
B) Add disable-model-invocation: true to the skill's frontmatter so only manual invocation triggers the lengthy dependency analysis.
C) Add context: fork to the skill's frontmatter so the analysis runs in an isolated subagent and only a summarized result is returned to the main conversation.
D) Add argument-hint: [directory] to the skill's frontmatter so the analysis only scans one directory at a time instead of the whole codebase.
correct_answers: C) Add context: fork to the skill's frontmatter so the analysis runs in an isolated subagent and only a summarized result is returned to the main conversation.
explanations: Incorrect. Restricting tool access changes which tools can run, not whether the resulting output pollutes the main conversation's context.
Incorrect. Preventing automatic invocation only changes who can trigger the skill; once invoked, the verbose output would still land directly in the main conversation.
Correct. context: fork runs the skill in an isolated subagent context; the verbose analysis stays in that forked context and only the returned result surfaces in the main conversation.
Incorrect. argument-hint only shows an autocomplete placeholder; it doesn't change scope of the scan or where the output lands.
